key_entities: AC reduction via ticket text rewrite
propositions: Pure prepacked single-pass verifier yields false-positive rejections when the evidence pack is incomplete; a hybrid filter+fallback approach (filter can only PASS or ABSTAIN, never reject, then narrow agentic verification to abstained ACs) eliminates false-positive rejections by construction.

Filter coverage is bimodal by AC style: ACs naming greppable artifacts (test functions, symbols, files) consistently PASS from static evidence packs (~90%), while ACs asserting runtime outcomes or store-side artifacts rationally ABSTAIN (~0%), yielding 39% coverage overall on real tickets.

Filter+fallback achieves -26% input tokens vs pure agentic (-46% on all-met tickets) with filter cost negligible (~0.4% of agentic spend); combined approach is cost-neutral-or-better while maintaining zero false PASSes on adversarial unmet criteria.

The criteria-reduction seam (patching ticket load to return AC block reduced to abstained-only ACs) automatically narrows the agentic verifier's step budget without code changes; mechanism works cleanly including epic child traversal.

False-positive rejection risk is eliminated by the hybrid design, but agentic false-FAIL variance on genuinely-met ACs persists at low rate (~2 of 7 in one run); productization should skip the filter for purely runtime-outcome AC styles where it abstains uniformly.
